name: Infiniti Q50 Red Sport 400
reliability: 6/10 — same VR30 under more stress; DAS steering quirks knock points off
cost_to_own: Insurance: High (400hp luxury sport sedan) · Maintenance ~$750/yr (premium fuel, perf brakes/tires)
popular_mods: Ecutek/JB4 tune (430+ whp with tune alone on the high-output VR30)
E85 + fuel system upgrades = 500-525 whp on stock turbos
Coilovers, sway bars, big brake kit
Best starting point in the Q50 range for a serious power build

generations.2016–2017 (Launch): Introduced alongside the 3.0t. 400hp from same VR30DDTT block with higher boost. Standard steer-by-wire DAS — controversial among enthusiasts.
generations.2018–2023 (Refresh): Same refresh as the 3.0t. More aggressive Red Sport-specific styling cues and Brembo brakes. Interior quality improved significantly.
generations.2024 (Final Year): Last production year. Discontinued alongside full Q50 lineup. Used copies remain one of the best performance sedan values on the used market.

common_issues: Steer-by-wire (DAS) feels numb — no road feedback at low speeds
Wastegate rattle (same as 3.0t — turbo housing wear)
Firm suspension transmits road harshness into the cabin
maintenance_tips: Same engine as 3.0t — follow same strict 5k oil change interval
DAS system can be replaced with a conventional rack if preferred
Inspect turbo boost hoses for cracks — high output puts more stress on them

engine.detail: High-output 3.0L VR30DDTT twin-turbo V6 — 400 hp and 350 lb-ft. Same Garrett turbos as the 300hp car but run harder (~14.5 psi) with an added optical turbine-speed sensor per turbo that lets them safely spin roughly 30% faster, plus extra charge-air-cooler pumping to manage the heat.
engine.watch: Same wastegate rattle as every VR30 — turbo-housing pivot wear. The extra boost and heat make strict 5,000-mile oil changes non-negotiable, and it's worth inspecting the boost hoses for cracks since high output stresses them more.

drivetrain.detail: Jatco 7-speed automatic, rear-drive or Intelligent AWD, sending the VR30's 350 lb-ft to the road.
drivetrain.watch: Valve-body issues and rear diff bushing wear are the high-mileage items shared with the 3.0t; keep the transmission fluid fresh rather than 'lifetime.'

suspension.detail: Sport-tuned double-wishbone front and multi-link rear, with standard steer-by-wire Direct Adaptive Steering.
suspension.watch: Two honest gripes: DAS feels numb with no road feedback at low speeds (it can be swapped for a conventional rack if you hate it), and the firm sport setup transmits road harshness into the cabin.

brakes.detail: Upgraded sport brake package — larger rotors with four-piston front calipers to match the extra power.
brakes.watch: Strong from the factory; fresh high-temp fluid and better pads are all that's needed before track use.

body.detail: Steel unibody sport sedan at about 3,890 lbs with Red Sport-specific styling.
body.watch: Standard age and use wear — rock chips, trim, seals; the biggest 'complaint' is really the firm ride, covered under suspension.
